cards.def: something an argument takes for granted without stating it
sentences: Which of the following is an underlying {assumption} of the argument above?
The plan rests on the {assumption} that prices will stay the same.
Her {assumption} that everyone had read the email turned out to be wrong.

cards.def: the main point that an argument is trying to prove
sentences: Which of the following best expresses the main {conclusion} of the argument?
The evidence does not support such a strong {conclusion}.
After weeks of testing, the scientists reached a surprising {conclusion}.

cards.def: to decide that something is true from the information you have
sentences: Which of the following can be reliably {inferred} from the passage?
From his silence, I {inferred} that he disagreed.
What can we {infer} about the author's opinion?

cards.def: a mistake or weakness in reasoning
sentences: Which of the following identifies the {flaw} in the argument?
The main {flaw} in his plan is that it ignores the cost.
There is a serious {flaw} in this reasoning.

cards.def: to make an argument less convincing
sentences: Which of the following, if true, would most {weaken} the argument?
This new evidence {weakens} the claim that the drug is safe.
One counterexample is enough to {weaken} a general rule.

cards.def: to make an argument more convincing
sentences: Which of the following, if true, would most {strengthen} the argument?
The survey results {strengthen} her case.
More data would {strengthen} the conclusion.

cards.def: to make something weaker or less effective, often indirectly
sentences: The small sample size {undermines} the study's findings.
Constant criticism can {undermine} a student's confidence.
Which statement would most seriously {undermine} the author's reasoning?

cards.def: a statement that something is true, which may not be proven
sentences: The author's {claim} is not supported by any evidence.
Some companies {claim} that their products are eco-friendly.
Which of the following is a {claim} made in the passage?

cards.def: facts that show whether something is true
sentences: There is no {evidence} that the new rule reduced accidents.
The {evidence} suggests a link between sleep and memory.
What {evidence} does the author give for this view?

cards.def: to suggest something without saying it directly
sentences: The author {implies} that the government acted too late.
Are you {implying} that I cheated?
What does the last sentence {imply}?

cards.def: connected to what is being discussed
sentences: Which piece of information is {relevant} to solving the problem?
His comment wasn't {relevant} to our discussion.
Only use the {relevant} data from the table.

cards.def: a general rule that guides decisions or reasoning
sentences: Which of the following best illustrates the {principle} behind the argument?
It's against my {principles} to lie.
The same {principle} applies to both cases.

cards.def: in agreement with something; not contradicting it
sentences: The results are {consistent} with our hypothesis.
Her story was not {consistent} with the facts.
Which statement is {consistent} with the data in the graph?

cards.def: to say or show the opposite of something
sentences: The second paragraph seems to {contradict} the first.
The new data {contradicts} earlier findings.
Try not to {contradict} yourself in the essay.

cards.def: based on good reasoning; logically correct
sentences: Is this a {valid} conclusion from the evidence given?
She made a {valid} point about the costs.
The argument is {valid}, but one of its premises is false.

cards.def: a statement an argument uses as a reason for its conclusion
sentences: If both {premises} are true, the conclusion must also be true.
The argument is built on a false {premise}.
Identify the {premise} that supports the final claim.

cards.def: a connection between two things that change together
sentences: A {correlation} between two things does not prove that one causes the other.
The study found a strong {correlation} between exercise and mood.
Is there any {correlation} between screen time and grades?

cards.def: a statement about a whole group based on only some examples
sentences: The argument makes a hasty {generalisation} from a single case.
It is an unfair {generalisation} to say that all teenagers are lazy.
Be careful with {generalisations} based on small samples.

cards.def: seeming reasonable and likely to be true
sentences: Which of the following is the most {plausible} explanation for the results?
His excuse sounded {plausible}, but I didn't believe it.
That is a {plausible} theory, but we need more evidence.

cards.def: able to be trusted
sentences: Is this website a {reliable} source of information?
The bus service here is not very {reliable}.
We need more {reliable} data before we decide.

cards.def: used to compare two facts that are different
sentences: Tom likes maths, {whereas} his brother prefers history.
Some species thrive in cities, {whereas} others disappear.
The first plan is cheap, {whereas} the second is fast.

cards.def: despite what has just been said
sentences: The test was difficult; {nevertheless}, most students passed.
It was raining, but we {nevertheless} went for a walk.
The plan is risky but {nevertheless} worth trying.

cards.def: for this reason; as a result
sentences: The road was closed, {hence} the delay.
Prices rose sharply; {hence}, fewer people could afford them.
The data is incomplete, and {hence} the conclusion is uncertain.

cards.def: only if
sentences: You can borrow the book {provided that} you return it by Friday.
The match will take place {provided that} the weather is good.
Anyone can join the club, {provided that} they attend every meeting.

cards.def: correct in every detail
sentences: Which of the following is an {accurate} description of the graph?
The thermometer gives an {accurate} reading.
His summary of the story was not quite {accurate}.

cards.def: to explain the reason for something, or to form part of a total
sentences: Which of the following would best {account for} the drop in sales?
Students {account for} almost half of the city's population.
How do you {account for} the difference between the two results?

cards.def: to be more important or greater than something else
sentences: The benefits of the new law {outweigh} its costs.
Do the risks {outweigh} the advantages?
For me, the low price {outweighs} the long delivery time.

cards.def: enough for a particular purpose
sentences: Is the information given {sufficient} to answer the question?
Passing the test is necessary but not {sufficient} for admission.
There wasn't {sufficient} time to finish the essay.

cards.def: a reason for disagreeing with something
sentences: Which of the following is the strongest {objection} to the proposal?
Nobody raised any {objection} to the plan.
Her main {objection} was the high cost.

cards.def: an unfair preference that affects judgement
sentences: The survey may show {bias} because only fans were asked.
Try to write the essay without {bias}.
Is there any evidence of {bias} in the article?

cards.def: large or important enough to have an effect
sentences: There was a {significant} increase in prices last year.
The difference between the two groups is not {significant}.
This discovery is {significant} for medicine.

cards.def: a limit on what is possible
sentences: Given these {constraints}, which timetable is possible?
Time is the main {constraint} on this project.
The budget {constraint} means we can only buy two laptops.

cards.def: a whole number that can be positive, negative or zero
sentences: If n is a positive {integer}, which of the following must be even?
−3, 0 and 7 are all {integers}.
Find the smallest {integer} greater than 2.5.

cards.def: the amount left over after division
sentences: When 17 is divided by 5, the {remainder} is 2.
What is the {remainder} when 100 is divided by 7?
A number leaves a {remainder} of 1 when divided by 4.

cards.def: able to be divided by a number with no remainder
sentences: Which of these numbers is {divisible} by 9?
A year is a leap year if it is {divisible} by 4, with some exceptions.
The sum of the digits is {divisible} by 3.

cards.def: a number that divides another number exactly
sentences: The {factors} of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.
3 is a {factor} of 27.
Find the highest common {factor} of 18 and 24.

cards.def: a number that is the result of multiplying a number by an integer
sentences: 15 and 30 are {multiples} of 5.
Find the least common {multiple} of 4 and 6.
How many {multiples} of 7 are there between 1 and 50?

cards.def: a number greater than 1 that divides only by 1 and itself
sentences: 2 is the only even {prime number}.
Is 91 a {prime number}?
Every integer greater than 1 is either a {prime number} or a product of primes.

cards.def: the number above the line in a fraction
sentences: In the fraction 3/4, the {numerator} is 3.
If you double the {numerator}, the fraction doubles.
The {numerator} and denominator have no common factor.

cards.def: the number below the line in a fraction
sentences: To add fractions, first find a common {denominator}.
In 5/8, the {denominator} is 8.
A fraction is undefined when its {denominator} is zero.

cards.def: the result of dividing one number by another
sentences: The {quotient} of 20 and 4 is 5.
Find the {quotient} when x² − 1 is divided by x − 1.
The {quotient} is 12 and the remainder is 3.

cards.def: the result of multiplying numbers
sentences: The {product} of two negative numbers is positive.
What is the {product} of 6 and 7?
The sum of two numbers is 10 and their {product} is 21.

cards.def: the result of subtracting one number from another
sentences: The {difference} between 15 and 9 is 6.
The sum of two numbers is 20 and their {difference} is 4.
Find the positive {difference} between the two roots.

cards.def: the sum of the values divided by how many values there are
sentences: The {mean} of 4, 6 and 11 is 7.
If the {mean} score of 5 students is 70, what is their total score?
Adding one very large value increases the {mean} a lot.

cards.def: the middle value when the numbers are put in order
sentences: The {median} of 3, 8, 9, 12 and 20 is 9.
The {median} is less affected by extreme values than the mean.
Find the {median} of the data in the table.

cards.def: the difference between the largest and smallest values
sentences: The {range} of 2, 7 and 15 is 13.
The temperatures had a {range} of 12 degrees that week.
Which data set has the largest {range}?

cards.def: a comparison of two amounts, such as 2 : 3
sentences: The {ratio} of boys to girls in the class is 3 : 4.
Divide 60 in the {ratio} 1 : 2.
The {ratio} of width to height is always the same.

cards.def: a part of a whole, compared with the whole
sentences: What {proportion} of the students passed the test?
The {proportion} of adults who smoke has fallen.
A large {proportion} of the budget goes on salaries.

cards.def: the difference between two percentages: from 20% to 25% is 5 of these
sentences: Unemployment rose from 5% to 7%, an increase of two {percentage points}.
The party's support fell by three {percentage points}.
A rise from 10% to 15% is five {percentage points}, but a 50% increase.

cards.def: when one quantity doubles, the other halves
sentences: For a fixed distance, speed and travel time are {inversely proportional}.
Pressure is {inversely proportional} to volume at constant temperature.
If y is {inversely proportional} to x, then xy is constant.

cards.def: in the same order as the things just mentioned
sentences: Anna and Ben are 12 and 15 years old, {respectively}.
The two angles are 40° and 60°, {respectively}.
The prices of tea and coffee are 300 and 500 tenge, {respectively}.

cards.def: to be greater than a number or amount
sentences: The total cost must not {exceed} 5000 tenge.
In how many months did sales {exceed} 1000 units?
The answer cannot {exceed} 100.

cards.def: not less than
sentences: You need {at least} 60 points in each section.
Each box contains {at least} three red balls.
How many socks must you take out to be sure of getting {at least} one pair?

cards.def: not more than
sentences: Each student may choose {at most} two subjects.
The bag can hold {at most} 5 kg.
There are {at most} four possible answers.

cards.def: following one after another without a gap
sentences: The sum of three {consecutive} integers is 48.
It rained for five {consecutive} days.
The product of two {consecutive} integers is always even.

cards.def: to find an approximate value
sentences: {Estimate} the answer before you calculate it.
Which of the following is the best {estimate} of the total?
Round each number to {estimate} the sum quickly.

cards.def: how likely something is to happen, from 0 to 1
sentences: The {probability} of rolling a six is 1/6.
What is the {probability} that both coins land heads?
The {probability} of rain tomorrow is 30%.

cards.def: money paid for borrowing or saving money
sentences: The bank pays 5% {interest} per year on savings.
Compound {interest} is calculated on the previous year's total.
How much {interest} will she pay on the loan?

cards.def: a reduction in price
sentences: The shop offers a 15% {discount} on all shoes.
After a {discount} of 20%, the jacket costs 8000 tenge.
Two {discounts} of 10% are not the same as one of 20%.

cards.def: meeting another line at 90°
sentences: The two lines are {perpendicular}, so they meet at a right angle.
Draw a line {perpendicular} to AB through point C.
The slopes of {perpendicular} lines multiply to −1.

cards.def: the distance around a circle
sentences: The {circumference} of a circle is 2πr.
The wheel has a {circumference} of 2 metres.
Find the {circumference} of a circle with diameter 10 cm.

cards.def: having all sides equal
sentences: All angles of an {equilateral} triangle are 60°.
The tile is an {equilateral} triangle with side 4 cm.
Is every {equilateral} triangle also isosceles?

cards.def: (of a triangle) having two equal sides
sentences: An {isosceles} triangle has two equal sides.
The base angles of an {isosceles} triangle are equal.
Triangle ABC is {isosceles} with AB = AC.

cards.def: a fixed line on a graph used to measure position
sentences: Time is shown on the horizontal {axis}.
The graph crosses the x-{axis} at 3.
Label both {axes} before plotting the points.

cards.def: a number that gives the original number when multiplied by itself
sentences: The {square root} of 81 is 9.
Which integer is closest to the {square root} of 50?
Take the {square root} of both sides of the equation.

ауа райына байланысты — в связи с погодой
